# splunkctl

> Open-source MCP server and CLI for Splunk Enterprise SIEM and Splunk SOAR. Give AI agents access to 238 Splunk commands via Model Context Protocol, or operate your instances as code from the terminal.

- [Home](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/): Open-source MCP server and CLI for Splunk Enterprise SIEM and Splunk SOAR. One tool, two interfaces — operate your Splunk environment from any AI

## Getting started

- [MCP server](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/mcp): Use splunkctl as a Model Context Protocol server to give AI agents — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or any MCP client — direct access
- [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/install): This pulls the forked SDK (splunkctl branch) automatically as a dependency.
- [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/configure): Prompts for host, port, auth method (token or username/password), tests the connection, and writes ~/.splunkctl/config.yaml with 0600 permissions.
- [Doctor](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/doctor): Diagnose connection, authentication, server health, and user permissions in a single command.

## Commands

- [Search](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/search): Run SPL queries against a remote Splunk instance from your laptop. This is the primary interface for threat hunting, incident response, and ad-hoc
- [Detection rules](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/rules): so they can live in git, pass through CI, and deploy across instances.
- [Alerts](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/alerts): Fired alerts are the SOC's incoming work queue. During an incident, you need to see what triggered, when, and at what severity. During planned
- [Dashboards](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/dashboards): Uses the Dashboard/Dashboards entity classes from the SDK fork.
- [Indexes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/indexes): Create, configure, and manage Splunk indexes.
- [Inputs](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/inputs): Manage monitor, TCP, UDP, script, and HTTP data inputs.
- [Lookups](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/lookups): Lookups turn raw events into actionable intelligence. SecOps teams use them for threat intel enrichment (IoC feeds correlated at search time),
- [HEC tokens](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/hec): HEC (HTTP Event Collector) is Splunk's HTTP/JSON ingestion endpoint. SecOps teams use it to push data into Splunk from sources that do not have a
- [Parsers](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/parsers): Manage source types (props.conf) and field extractions (transforms.conf) via the REST API.
- [Macros, eventtypes, tags](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/knowledge): Friendly, object-shaped verbs over macros.conf, eventtypes.conf, and
- [Conf editor](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/conf): Generic conf file/stanza editor over the REST confs API — the escape hatch for any Splunk conf file that doesn't have a dedicated command group yet:
- [Apps](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/apps): Splunk's detection and enrichment capabilities live in apps -- Technology Add-ons (TAs) for data normalization, security content packs like Splunk
- [Users & roles](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/users): Manage Splunk users and roles via the REST API.

## Operations

- [State (config-as-code)](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/state): snapshot of an instance's detection content, edit it like code, diff it against the live instance, then push -- with a savable before→after JSON
- [ES notables](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/es): The SOC daily loop: see what's queued, pull the full detail on one notable, then assign, set status/urgency/disposition, or leave a comment — alone
- [KV store](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/kvstore): Splunk's KV store backs allowlists, threat-intel feeds, and Enterprise Security's asset/identity tables — schema-less JSON document storage scoped
- [Data models](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/datamodels): Mature SOC detections run on accelerated CIM data models via | tstats — this group answers "which models exist," "is acceleration healthy," and
- [Audit & RBAC](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/audit): Regulator-facing evidence for bank SOC operations: who changed what (audit changes) and who can do what (audit rbac). Both commands are read-only —
- [Server health](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/server): System health, license, KV store status, and topology health reads.

## SOAR

- [Overview](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar): Platform reads, containers, artifacts, playbooks, and actions on Splunk SOAR (on-premises or cloud) via the REST API.
- [Apps, assets & ingest](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-automation): Apps, assets, connectivity testing, and ingestion monitoring on Splunk SOAR. Companion to soar.md (platform reads, containers, artifacts, vault,
- [Playbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-playbooks): Playbook lifecycle and playbooks-as-code workflow on Splunk SOAR via the REST API. Export, edit in git, import back -- the first programmatic
- [Actions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-actions): Run, monitor, and inspect action runs on Splunk SOAR assets.
- [Functions](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-functions): Manage SOAR custom functions: list, inspect, import, export, update, and delete. Custom functions are reusable Python snippets called from playbook
- [Cases & workbooks](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-cases): Promote containers to cases with workbook templates, view phase/task structure, and manage individual phases and tasks. Cases are containers with
- [Approvals](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-approvals): Manage approval requests from SOAR playbook prompt blocks. A playbook pauses at a prompt action and waits for an external approve/deny response
- [Custom lists](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-lists): Manage SOAR custom lists (the decided_list API). Custom lists are simple tabular data structures stored as an array of rows, where each row is an
- [Indicators & evidence](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-indicators): IOC indicator lookups and evidence management on Splunk SOAR.
- [Users, roles & audit](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-admin): Manage SOAR platform users, inspect role permissions, and query the audit trail. User mutations are guarded (dry-run by default, --yes to apply).
- [Ingest (SIEM to SOAR)](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/soar-ingest): Ingest SIEM search results into Splunk SOAR as containers and artifacts, using the official CIM-to-CEF field mapping and connector conventions.
